title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — if omit hereditary: not from Adam–Christ collation
pass_a_gloss: Say he skipped hereditary corruption, and two consequences land. One: you cannot pull it from Paul's whole first-Adam / second-Adam collation. Later verses name no other Adam-evils into the race than v. 12 already listed—music to Pighius's ears.
pass_b_english: For if you shall say that he passed over hereditary corruption, two things will follow: One, that it cannot be gathered from this whole collation which the Apostle instituted between the first and the second Adam. For in the following verses he does not teach that other evils flowed from Adam into the human race than those which he named in this v. 12. But that will greatly help Pighius's cause.
source_text: Nam, si dixeris eum corruptionem haereditariam praetermisisse, sequentur duo: Unum, eam ex hac tota collatione, quam inter primum & secundum Adamum Apostolus instituit, colligi non posse. Non enim alia mala ex Adamo in genus humanum manasse sequentibus versibus docet, quam quae hoc v. 12. nominavit. Id autem Pighii causam valde iuvabit.

lemmas.gloss: collation of first and second Adam

choices.choice: Omit hereditary → not from Rom 5 Adam–Christ collation; helps Pighius
